previous.description: A dotnet tool that reads a .NET test report and answers why the tests failed - for xUnit, NUnit, MSTest, TUnit, Reqnroll and LightBDD runs, for people and for AI agents - without loading the file: `kronikol query failures` is usually the whole answer, `repro` is the dotnet test --filter line that re-runs each failure. Command-line companion for Kronikol. Includes `kronikol merge`, which combines several mergeable TestRunReport.json files (produced with GenerateMergeableData enabled — e.g. by parallel CI runners) into a single combined TestRunReport.html plus the merged TestRunReport.json beside it, so a sharded run is queryable and can serve as a baseline; `kronikol ingest`, which replays language-neutral NDJSON interaction captures (from an out-of-process proxy tap or any non-.NET capturer) into a full Kronikol report; `kronikol query`, which answers questions about a TestRunReport.json — why a test failed, what a service returned, where a wrong value came from — without loading the file, so a 10 MB report is debuggable by tooling and by AI agents; `kronikol export`, which pushes NDJSON interaction captures to an OTLP/HTTP collector as OpenTelemetry spans so the traffic only Kronikol saw appears in Tempo/Jaeger next to the app's real traces; `kronikol ctrf`, which converts a TestRunReport.json into a Common Test Report Format document so CI tooling that already speaks CTRF can read a Kronikol run; and `kronikol init-agents`, which installs the test-debugging skill and the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md instruction block into an existing repository, so its agents know the report is there and how to read it.
